result.detail: Known deviations: (1) The held AW and W registers are reset, which the microarchitecture marks as unnecessary. This is harmless. (2) The next-state block assigns some variables more than once to get last-assignment-wins priority, as the microarchitecture specifies. This goes beyond the default-then-override style rule. (3) The interface spec's formal proof item is not covered here, because the task asks only for rtl_source and testbench. (4) A simultaneous read and write on the same clock is not driven in the directed tests, but the two directions are independent in the RTL. Under Verilator, the default runtime error limit stops the simulation at the first $error. A failing run therefore ends without printing a verdict, and it still counts as a failure.
